key_insight: Selecting ties—equally preferred response pairs—by predicted influence can reduce spurious reliance with fewer examples than uniform tie selection.
engineering_relevance: Targeted tie augmentation can make preference optimization more data-efficient when mitigating unwanted correlations.
method: Derive tie influence for log-linear policies; selecting the largest predicted reductions is first-order optimal for fixed-size subsets.
Characterize when absolute implicit reward margin is a useful proxy for influence.
Estimate influence using a counterfactual spurious-reliance proxy and generalized Gauss–Newton curvature for language models.
evidence_signal: Across log-linear policies, neural models, and large language models, the selection rules consistently achieved comparable reductions in spurious reliance with fewer ties than uniform selection.
watch_item: Exact influence requires spurious-feature knowledge and objective curvature; reward-margin ranking is a proxy whose usefulness depends on specific conditions.
paper_title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
